description: Classifies min-N=30 as a general feature-independent descriptive floor (not a validity claim), defines eligible/limited/unavailable/requires-review criteria, ratifies the 75 approved groups, ARG13/ARG19 unavailability, and the fallback hierarchy with disclosure.

statements.statement: For v0.1 descriptive reference distributions, effective N >= 30 after duplicate policy is a general feature-independent eligibility floor.
N >= 30 establishes no statistical validity or normative sufficiency; normative interpretation remains blocked by the validated-measurement gate.
A group is ELIGIBLE when approved, effective N >= 30, complete-case N >= 30, feature version matches, distribution exists, and no degenerate flag, for descriptive reference purposes.
Groups with missingness flags, degenerate distributions, or fragile entry-year sizes (2003/2007) are LIMITED and must disclose their limitation.
ARG13 and ARG19 standalone distributions are UNAVAILABLE; their documents remain in broader approved groups.
Any group with effective N < 30 after duplicate policy, unknown ids, missing distributions, or feature/version mismatch is UNAVAILABLE; silent group widening is forbidden.
The fallback hierarchy prompt+timed -> prompt -> genre+timed -> genre -> UNAVAILABLE is ratified with mandatory requested/resolved/disclosure reporting.
Fallback to a genre-level group without prompt control is descriptive only and is not a prompt-controlled comparison.
Any use outside the descriptive reference purpose (normative interpretation, learner-facing output, cross-version comparisons, model development, frequency-resource features) requires review.
Raising or lowering the floor, feature-dependent floors, or changing the fallback hierarchy require a major policy amendment with methodological review.
